text:
maria_support: FYI customer (Acme Retail) escalated — rerank endpoint returning scores that end up sorting incorrectly in their frontend.

maria_support: Example from their TS client (they pasted request/response):
```json
{
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "a", "text": "foo" },
    { "id": "b", "text": "bar" }
  ],
  "scores": [ "0.00000\u0000", "1e-06" ]
}
```

maria_support: They say frontend sorts lexicographically because scores came back as strings, and sometimes parseFloat returns NaN for entries with trailing \u0000.

jamal_engineer: Oof. do we have server logs for that thread id? Any 4xx from our rerank handler?

maria_support: Customer provided server response snippet: 200 OK but body contains scores as strings: `["0.00000\u0000","1e-06"]`. No 4xx.

sophia_ml: Interesting — our API normally emits numbers, not strings. Could be an SDK serialization issue (TS or Python client).

oliver_tsdev: @maria_support can you ask for the exact SDK versions? TS SDK v1.3.2 reported. Also, do they use any custom Buffer/encoding middleware?

maria_support: They replied: Node 18, ts-sdk@1.3.2, no custom middleware. Repro repo attached (minimal).

ryan_support: repro steps they sent (condensed):
1) npm i ts-sdk@1.3.2
2) send rerank with candidates + scores generated from a native scoring lib (was using Buffer -> base64 intermediate)
3) server returns JSON containing score strings with trailing null bytes and occasional exponent strings.

maria_support: They pasted server raw body (escaped): `"scores":["0.00000\u0000","1e-06"]` and frontend sorts as strings => wrong ordering.

jamal_engineer: I pulled the repro. Quick check: when we stringify a Buffer in some codepaths it can include embedded NULs if not trimmed. Looks like ts-sdk serializer ends up doing toString('utf8') on a fixed-size Buffer that had padding. That could append `\u0000`. Then we serialize as JSON strings (not numbers).

oliver_tsdev: Confirmed. In legacy code path for rerank payload we do: `const s = buf.toString(); obj.scores.push(s);` and assume downstream will parse. For numeric scores we should coerce to Number and strip nulls.

sophia_ml: Why did Python customers not hit this? Python SDK uses float array -> json numbers. Only happens when user supplies pre-encoded score buffers via ts-sdk helper.

maria_support: Customer also reported another odd case: sometimes server returns exponents as strings (`"1e-06"`). That one is safe if parsed, but trailing nulls break parseFloat.

jamal_engineer: I created an internal repro: Node Buffer of length 8 with padding -> toString() yields '0.00000\u0000'. parseFloat('0.00000\u0000') => 0 (ok in Node), but in browser parseFloat may return NaN if embedded control char present. So frontend brittle.

oliver_tsdev: Quick mitigation: server will accept numeric strings and coerce to numbers before returning (fallback) and log occurrences. I'll open a hotfix to coerce and strip ASCII \u0000 on the API layer. Deploy-bot will run a patch job.

deploy-bot: deploy start: api-rerank-coerce-2171 -> staging (canary 10%).

jamal_engineer: Longer term: patch ts-sdk (PR #4567) — ensure serializer: trim null bytes, and always emit numbers for score arrays (Number(s) or parseFloat after cleaning). Also add unit + e2e tests exercising padded Buffers.

oliver_tsdev: Draft PR ready, adding a patch release 1.3.3. Also will add a runtime warning if SDK detects non-numeric score strings.

maria_support: Customer notified of temporary server-side coercion. They confirmed frontend will be patched to parse numbers but asked for SDK patch ETA.

oliver_tsdev: Targeting release tomorrow morning PST. Will include changelog entry 'fix: trim null bytes and coerce score types in rerank payload'.

maria_support: Customer happy with timeline, will test with canary release and confirm. :thumbsup:

ryan_support: Follow-ups: log occurrences per-customer so we can alert if any other customers hit same issue. Also add a KB note for support on how to triage malformed score arrays (strip control chars, check SDK version).

sophia_ml: Filed an ML follow-up to ensure any scoring libs that emit fixed-width binary outputs are documented.

maria_support: closing loop when customer verifies. Thanks all.
